prune_scope_hazard.finding: In game-dev-2d-shokunin, `git worktree prune` is NOT target-selective. `git -C game-dev-2d-shokunin worktree prune --dry-run -v` proposes removing FIVE registrations in one pass: r80-baseline-frozen-worktree, r81-frozen, game-dev-2d-shokunin-wt-r98, -wt-r99, -wt-r100.
prune_scope_hazard.why_it_matters: Three of those five (wt-r98/99/100) are NOT-SAFE: each named branch carries 1 unpushed commit. A blanket prune in this repo would discard those registrations while the branch commits are still unpublished.
prune_scope_hazard.object_loss_check: None of the five SHAs is lost by pruning: `log --oneline <sha> --not --all | wc -l` -> 0 for all five (68bee6e7, fe1a996e, 2d562282, d9320ddf, 27f465c6), and refs/heads/wt-r98|wt-r99|wt-r100 survive the prune (proved read-only: for-each-ref refs/heads still lists all four branches). The damage from a blanket prune is loss of the worktree registrations, not of commits.
prune_scope_hazard.recommendation: Execute this ticket with a targeted removal, not a repo-wide prune, e.g. `git -C game-dev-2d-shokunin worktree remove --force /tmp/r81-frozen` (or prune only after the wt-r98/99/100 branches are pushed). Do NOT run bare `git worktree prune` in game-dev-2d-shokunin.

recommended_command_validated.why: The go/no-go asks for a TARGETED removal instead of a repo-wide prune. That claim is not asserted from the docs alone.
recommended_command_validated.method: Ran the command against a throwaway git repo built with mktemp -d (/tmp/s42-cmdtest.X9Al), never against the fleet: git init base; git worktree add --detach ../wt1 HEAD; git worktree add --detach ../wt2 HEAD; rm -rf ../wt1.
recommended_command_validated.observed: git -C base worktree list -> wt1 'prunable', wt2 healthy. `git worktree remove --force ../wt1` -> exit 0, no error, despite the dir being absent. After: worktree list shows only base + wt2; ../wt2 still exists on disk.
recommended_command_validated.conclusion: Targeted removal of a dir-absent prunable registration succeeds and leaves sibling registrations untouched - the recommended command is correct and the blanket-prune hazard is avoidable. Nothing in the fleet was mutated (throwaway repo under /tmp, since deleted by mktemp lifecycle).
